title: Industry Pulse — AI / Agent Ecosystem

bullets.title: Claude Sonnet 5 goes GA — Anthropic's most agentic Sonnet, near-Opus-4.8 performance at $2/$10 per 1M intro pricing
bullets.summary: Launched June 30 as the default model for Free/Pro (available to Max/Team/Enterprise), Sonnet 5 plans, drives browsers and terminals, and runs autonomously at a level that recently required larger models, at $2/$10 per 1M tokens through Aug 31 (then $3/$15); safety evals show fewer undesirable behaviors than Sonnet 4.6 in agentic contexts.
bullets.how: The cost floor dropping under The Construct: route high-volume routine jobs (daily scans, drafting, browser ops) to Sonnet 5 and reserve Fable 5 credits for long-autonomy reasoning — the intro-pricing window is a free margin experiment through August.

bullets.title: Claude Enterprise adds admin analytics, model-level entitlements, and spend alerts
bullets.summary: Early-July release notes add richer usage/cost/productivity analytics for admins, per-model access controls, and alerts to avoid surprise overages.
bullets.how: With Fable 5 moving to usage credits after July 7 and Sonnet 5 repricing in September, this is exactly the governance tooling to watch; also a feature PRAGMA can point client orgs at when deploying agent fleets on their Claude tenancy.

bullets.title: Microsoft stands up 'Frontier Company' — $2.5B and ~6,000 forward-deployed engineers; ServiceNow + Accenture launch a parallel program
bullets.summary: Microsoft's new operating unit embeds engineers, industry specialists, and salespeople directly inside enterprise clients to co-design, deploy, and optimize AI systems at scale, the same week ServiceNow and Accenture announced a forward-deployed engineering program for agentic AI.
bullets.how: Strongest validation yet of PRAGMA's AI-operator consulting wedge: the giants are industrializing 'humans who deploy agents' for the Fortune 500, leaving the SMB/mid-market tier wide open for PRAGMA to own with faster, cheaper, agent-first delivery.

bullets.title: Profound ships 'Aim' — an always-on background agent that turns AI-search visibility signals into prioritized marketing work
bullets.summary: Announced July 2, Aim continuously monitors prompt trends, AI citations, sentiment, and competitive benchmarks across AI search and converts them into a prioritized workstream for marketing teams.
bullets.how: A funded competitor in exactly the PRAGMA Mirror lane (consumer-LLM brand-visibility scanning → action); study its signal taxonomy and sharpen Mirror's differentiator: we don't just report visibility, our agents (Pulse) execute the fixes on the client's owned presence.

bullets.title: arXiv: 'From Question Answering to Task Completion: A Survey on Agent System and Harness Design'
bullets.summary: Surveys how agent capability increasingly comes from harness design (orchestration, tool interfaces, memory, verification loops) rather than the base model alone, mapping the design space from QA-style assistants to full task-completion systems.
bullets.how: A direct framework for The Construct's architecture reviews: our edge is the harness (locked rules, PRAXIS, memory tiers, scheduled scans) — use it to audit each agent's orchestration/verification loop as models commoditize.

praxis_lesson: The week's pattern is value migrating from models to deployment: Sonnet 5 collapses the price of agentic capability while Microsoft ($2.5B, 6,000 people) and Accenture/ServiceNow industrialize forward-deployed AI operators for enterprises. PRAGMA's move is to be the forward-deployed operator for the SMB/mid-market tier the giants won't touch — cheaper substrate widens our margins, and the harness/governance layer we already run is the defensible part.
